title: BC Home Owner Grant: Amounts, Eligibility And How To Apply
summary: Learn who qualifies for the BC home owner grant, how to apply, what the 2026 amounts mean for your budget, and what changes in 2027.
body_markdown:
You have worked your mortgage payment into your budget, then the property tax notice arrives. Before setting that bill aside, it is worth checking whether the BC home owner grant can help.


How much could you claim? Does your lender take care of it? And what happens if you have just bought the home or missed the tax due date?


Let's look at the eligibility rules, a simple budgeting example and the application steps. The figures below were checked in November 2026, with the January 2027 change identified separately.


## What Is The BC Home Owner Grant?


Simply put, the **BC home owner grant** reduces annual property taxes on an eligible principal residence. It applies to homeowners paying municipal or provincial rural property taxes; if you pay a First Nation, contact that First Nation about its equivalent benefit. See the[Province's grant overview](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/taxes/property-taxes/annual-property-tax/home-owner-grant) .


Think of it as one part of your ongoing ownership budget. If you are[buying your first home](https://breezeful.com/blog/ca/first-time-home-buyer-in-canada/) , keep this annual expense on your checklist alongside the mortgage, utilities and maintenance. Start with the actual tax notice, then work through the relief you may qualify for.


## Who Can Qualify?


The Province's[eligibility rules](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/taxes/property-taxes/annual-property-tax/home-owner-grant) generally require you to be the registered owner, a Canadian citizen or permanent resident, live in B.C. and occupy the property as your principal residence. First-time buyer status is not a requirement. Special rules cover circumstances such as an owner's death or a temporary absence.


For homeowners turning **65 or older during the year** , the[seniors' grant rules](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/taxes/property-taxes/annual-property-tax/home-owner-grant/senior) may allow a higher amount. The qualifying senior must be the applicant. Eligible veterans, people with disabilities and some other households may also qualify for additional assistance, subject to the[Province's programme requirements](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/taxes/property-taxes/annual-property-tax/home-owner-grant) .


## How Much Can You Claim In 2026?


These are the maximum amounts in the[Province's 2026 announcement](https://news.gov.bc.ca/releases/2025FIN0049-001293) . Your eligibility, assessed value and tax bill determine the actual grant.


Property Location Regular Grant Total Additional Grant, If Eligible


Capital, Metro Vancouver or Fraser Valley regional districts $570 $845


Other areas of B.C. $770 $1,045


For 2026, the full-grant assessment threshold is **$2,075,000** . Above that, the grant decreases by $5 for each $1,000 of assessed value over the threshold, according to the same[provincial announcement](https://news.gov.bc.ca/releases/2025FIN0049-001293) .


The grant also leaves a minimum tax amount payable: **$350 for the regular grant or $100 for the additional grant** . The[City of Richmond's explanation](https://www.richmond.ca/city-hall/finance/rates/homegrant.htm) outlines these limits. A small tax bill can therefore mean a smaller grant.


**Planning for 2027?** Effective January 1, the northern and rural $200 benefit ends. The Province lists a[regular grant of $570 across B.C.](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/taxes/property-taxes/annual-property-tax/home-owner-grant) and a[total seniors' grant of $845 across B.C.](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/taxes/property-taxes/annual-property-tax/home-owner-grant/senior) . Check the applicable year's assessment threshold when preparing next year's budget.


## What Would The Savings Look Like?


Let's say you own and live in a Vancouver home assessed at $1,000,000. For this **hypothetical 2026 example** , assume you meet all regular-grant requirements, no grant has already been claimed, and your eligible annual property taxes are $4,000 CAD before the grant.


Using the[2026 regular amount of $570](https://news.gov.bc.ca/releases/2025FIN0049-001293) , the calculation is $4,000 − $570 = **$3,430 remaining for the year** . That remains above the $350 minimum tax amount.


For a personal savings plan, $3,430 divided by 12 is about **$285.83 per month** , compared with $333.33 before the grant. That is a $47.50 monthly difference. This is budgeting arithmetic, not a quoted lender payment or permission to pay the tax bill monthly.


Keep the two questions separate: how much should you set aside, and when must the bill be paid? A monthly savings habit can help with the first; your tax notice answers the second.


## How Do You Apply?


You must apply every year, including when your financial institution pays the property taxes for you. **Your lender does not apply for the grant on your behalf.** The Province's[application guide](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/taxes/property-taxes/annual-property-tax/home-owner-grant/apply) sets out the process:


1. Have your property's jurisdiction and roll numbers ready, along with your Social Insurance Number. The property numbers appear on your tax or BC Assessment notice.
2. Apply through the provincial website or by phone at 1-888-355-2700. Service BC can assist if you lack computer or internet access.
3. Keep your confirmation number so you can check the application status.


The recommended window is after receiving your property tax notice and before its payment due date. If your lender collects money for taxes, ask how the grant is reflected in that arrangement. Keep the application confirmation with your tax records.


## What Are The Potential Pitfalls?


**Confusing the year-end deadline with the payment deadline.** You can apply until December 31 of the current tax year, but applying after your property tax due date may leave late-payment penalties on the unpaid amount. Check the[provincial timing rules](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/taxes/property-taxes/annual-property-tax/home-owner-grant/apply) .


**Assuming a purchase creates another grant.** Under the[buying and selling rules](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/taxes/property-taxes/annual-property-tax/home-owner-grant) , a buyer must check that the previous owner has not claimed for that property and that the buyer has not received a grant elsewhere that year. You must occupy the home when applying.


**Writing off a missed year without checking.** A[retroactive application](https://www2.gov.bc.ca/gov/content/taxes/property-taxes/annual-property-tax/home-owner-grant/retroactive) may be possible for the previous year. You must have qualified on December 31 of that year, still own the property and meet the other conditions. For a missed 2025 grant, the application must be received by December 31, 2026.


## Does The Grant Fit Into Your Homeownership Budget?


The grant can leave more room in your annual budget, but build your plan around confirmed eligibility and the correct tax year. Do your homework before counting on the maximum amount, especially after moving or when planning for 2027.


As you review[ways to manage costs as a new homeowner](https://breezeful.com/blog/ca/5-tips-for-saving-money-as-a-new-homeowner/) , put your tax notice and grant confirmation beside your mortgage statement. Crunch the numbers together.
